newsitem.title: UK: British output, manufacturing picks up in July.
newsitem.headline: British output, manufacturing picks up in July.

text.p: British industrial output and manufacturing production rose modestly in July, backing the view economic growth will accelerate in the second half of 1996.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said overall output and manufacturing both rose by 0.5 percent during the month, after falls in both sectors during June.
On a year-on-year basis, industrial output was up by 0.9 percent while manufacturing rose by 0.3 percent. This compared with monthly falls of 0.9 and 0.1 percent in June respectively.
The figures were in line with expectations and backed the view that economic growth will accelerate sharply in the second half of 1996, boosted by both domestic demand and output.
"Manufacturing prospects for the second half of 1996 are good," British Treasury Economics Secretary Angela Knight said.
